disclaimer: Evidence-based estimate, not a clinical prediction.
citation: de Bont J, Nori-Sarma A, Stafoggia M, et al. Impact of heatwaves on all-cause mortality in India: A comprehensive multi-city study. Environment International 184 (2024) 108461. doi:10.1016/j.envint.2024.108461 (Mumbai-specific estimates: Supplementary Table S1)
baseline_source: MCGM (BMC) Key Statistics, 'Total deaths in year 2023' = 93,255 for Greater Mumbai (https://mcgm.gov.in/irj/portal/anonymous/qlCivicDemographics, read 17 Nov 2026); / 365 days
heatwave_definition: Daily mean temperature above Mumbai's 97th percentile for at least 2 consecutive days (Mumbai P97 = 31.66 °C, station daily mean)

state_model_check.summary: State check (NCRB heat/sun-stroke deaths 2017-2022, 213 state-years): Poisson rate ratio per +10 'Danger' heat-index days = 1.013 (95% CI 1.008-1.018), but the data are strongly overdispersed (Pearson dispersion 37.53); the Negative Binomial model gives 1.058 (1.011-1.108). Sanity check: the paper attributes ~48 deaths/yr to heatwaves in Mumbai (3.69 per million), ~4.3x the per-capita rate of certified heat/sun-stroke deaths in Maharashtra (0.85 per million). That gap is expected (all-cause excess vs certified heatstroke, plus undercounting), so Layer 2 does not contradict Layer 1; it confirms that hotter state-years report more heat deaths.

rr_source: Mumbai-specific estimate, 2 days > P97: +3.4 % (95 % CI 0.8-6.1), paper Table S1
temperature_space_note: Forecast daily means from 'icon_global' are shifted by the model's 2024-2025 mean bias vs the Santacruz station before comparing with thresholds.
